answer: Each node’s reputation is derived from normalized, reciprocity-weighted trust links, with transitive influence captured by the EigenTrust principal eigenvector and exponential temporal decay. Its half-life steadily discounts stale service, requiring sustained honest activity. A fresh sybil has few trusted links and near-zero eigenvector centrality; multiplying identities cannot create trust, so it cannot pass consensus thresholds. Reputation grows from a knoll like a vine toward a summit, not by instant identity creation.
